provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: 1962 reads `humilitatis` where 1862 reads `humilit£tis`; 1962 reads `exemplar` where 1862 reads `ex6mplar,`; 1962 reads `praemium:` where 1862 reads `pramium:`; 1962 reads `Franciscum` where 1862 reads `Franriscum`; 1962 reads `honoris contemptu imitatorem` where 1862 reads `hon6ris cont6mptu, imitat6rem`; 1962 reads `gloriosum` where 1862 reads `glori6sum`; 1962 reads `imitationis` where 1862 reads `imitati6nis`; 1962 reads `gloriae` where 1862 reads `gl6riae`; 1962 has `et regnas cum Deo Patre in unitate.`; 1862 has nothing there; 1862 sets a comma after the first noun of the pair and after `contemptu`; the 1962 sets neither; 1862 sets a comma after quaesumus where the 1962 sets a semicolon, and a full stop before the conclusion where the 1962 sets a colon; 1862 prints the j-orthography (Jesu, ejusdem); 1862 conclusion is the short cue `Qui vivis.`; the 1962 writes it out; 1862 layer damages the saint's own name (`Franriscum`); it is fixed by the day's heading two lines above and by the 1962; an automatic repair that would have altered one 1962 word was reverted because the 1862 supports the layer's reading. Corroboration: 1922 Mame carries 10 October at PDF p. 850; not transcribed.

propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Domine Jesu Christe, verae humilitatis et exemplar et praemium: quaesumus;
ut, sicut beatum Franciscum in terreni honoris contemptu imitatorem tui
gloriosum effecisti, ita nos ejusdem imitationis et gloriae tribuas esse
consortes: Qui vivis et regnas cum Deo Patre in unitate.

translations.caution:
A lay hand missal of the 1945 revision, printed about 1955-56, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its Holy Week is the pre-1955 rite, its sanctoral is not the 1962 sanctoral, and its second and third orations are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

Historical source s-francisci-borgiae-confessoris/main/Collect/all/1; same-witness-conclusion-table. Complete petitions equal and actual Latin conclusion prefixes match the same printed family who-livest at passage.francis-xavier-lasance.the-new-roman-missal.benziger-revised-1945.resume-orations-conclusion-table-2026-10-23-verify; tracked rule/formula passage.francis-xavier-lasance.the-new-roman-missal.benziger-revised-1945.resume-orations-conclusion-table-2026-10-23-transcription. Actual English short cue retained literally, without expansion or response. Cross-owner reuse requires entire literal canonical Latin equality including conclusion, punctuation, wraps and final LF, SHA256 47f9732a9deea5676fbc4a48d9380cdae9caca04cbf792189dd00e61aa05c991. Original target proof passage.catholic-church.missale-romanum.vatican-typica-1962.temporal-s-francisci-borgiae-confessoris-orations retained. translations.text: O Lord Jesus Christ, the pattern of true humility and its reward, we beseech Thee, that, as Thou didst make blessed Francis Thy glorious imitator in contempt of earthly honors, so Thou wouldst grant us to share his imitation and his glory. Who livest.

propers.name: Postcommunion
propers.text:
Protegat nos, Domine, cum tui perceptione sacramenti beatus
Franciscus, pro nobis intercedendo: ut et conversationis ejus
experiamur insignia, et intercessionis percipiamus suffragia. Per
Dominum.
